game.name: Super Mario World
game.rules:
Please read the **Category Rules** by clicking on the tab on the top right once you have familiarized yourself with the **Game Rules** below.

## Leaderboard Verification Process

To allow the moderators of the Super Mario World leaderboard to verify your submission in a timely manner, please adhere to the following rules and guidelines. Please read and understand the sections below on: Submission Guidelines, General Rules, Platform Rules and High Level Run Rules. A run is considered a "high level run" when it crosses the millisecond threshold for its respective category.  Millisecond threshold times will be highlighted in each individual categories' rules section. High level runs will be reviewed more closely and may require additional time to verify.

## Submission Guidelines

- Submit with the correct run information (category, platform, game version, etc.)
- Game video and audio is recommended but not required for newer runners (even a phone recording is accepted as long as the gameplay is understandable)
- The submitted video should be highlighted and cut to show the run itself, long vods are discouraged and may lead to rejection. Showing a couple of seconds before the reset and showing the credits (as well as file check for Exit-oriented categories) is encouraged
- Do not use the LiveSplit finish time as your definitive run submission time, re-time your run and submit it with the correct hours, minutes, and seconds (and milliseconds if you meet the ms threshold)
- Correctly mark your run if it was run on a legal emulator, (VC is not emulator unless you're, for example, running WiiVC in Dolphin) hardware emulators such as SuperNT should be marked as emu runs.

Read more about the submission and verification process here: [https://www.speedrun.com/smw/forums/f7cr2](https://www.speedrun.com/smw/forums/f7cr2)

## General Rules

- No use of save states, restore points, or rewinding
- No speeding up or slowing down the game
- No cheats (e.g. Game Genie, Action Replay, emulator cheats)
- No memory viewing
- No turbo buttons
- No pressing Left + Right or Up + Down on the D-pad intentionally for any advantage
- Only bijectional remapping of buttons. This means that you may remap your controls, for example on the Nintendo Switch or emulator, but you can only map one key to any one button. You cannot map one key to simulate pressing more than one button, nor can you map multiple keys to the same button. **This rule does not apply for the 0 Exit category.**

## Platform Rules

- The following platforms are **allowed**: SFC/SNES, Virtual Console (WiiVC, 3DSVC, WiiUVC), SNES Classic, Nintendo Switch Online (not the "SP" version), SuperNT, MiSTer and various emulators
- The following emulators are **allowed** for all categories: Snes9x v1.5x and higher, bsnes Compatibility Core (Bizhawk, Higan, lsnes) and Mesen-S
- The following emulators are **allowed** for all categories **except** for 0 Exit and 11 Exit Cloud: ZSNES, no$sns, bsnes Performance Core (Bizhawk, Higan). These emulators are not accurate enough to properly emulate open bus behavior, which is required for certain item swap glitches.

Read more about valid platforms and emulators rules here: [https://www.speedrun.com/smw/forums/8w7yc](https://www.speedrun.com/smw/forums/8w7yc)

## High Level Run Rules

If your run meets the millisecond threshold for its given category, your run will be considered a High Level Run. High level runs are subject to additional scrutiny by the moderators, and the responsibility will be on the runner to prove their legitimacy by following as much of the additional rules and recommendations below as possible.

- Clear game video and audio is **required**. Make sure that there are no technical issues with the game feed, and that the game audio is clearly audible. The gameplay being obstructively covered or loud music over the game audio can lead to rejection
- It is **highly recommended** for a runner of top-level skill, or possibly on WR pace attempts to stream their attempts or have a history of streaming. This is to give more validity to a runner's skill if it is called into question due to suspected suspicious behaviour during runs. If you are not able to stream, ensure that you have a sufficient backlog of locally recorded attempts that you can provide as proof to show that your run is legitimate.
- It is **recommended** to submit your LiveSplit file (of .lss extension) along with your run using splits.io
- For high level emulator runners, it is **required** to turn on the input display. It is **recommended** to turn on and display the frame counter, as well as the FPS.
- For high level emulator runners, it is **lightly recommended** to capture the entire emulator window, meaning the emulator's title bar and menu bar as well as the entire game. This is seen as a more extreme showing of proof for emulator runners and can make a runner's stream look less appealing, so only follow this recommendation if you feel that you are not able to follow multiple of the above recommendations.
- It is **lightly recommended** to get yourself acquainted with using [therun.gg](https://therun.gg) for the purpose of connecting your LiveSplit program to the site to be able to show detailed data of your runs and attempts, as another way to provide validity to your runs.

If a runner is contacted about their submission, they will be expected to work with the mods and provide more proof if enough is not available. If the moderators do not believe that sufficient proof of skill is provided due to the above criteria not being met, they may reject the run.

Leaderboard verification process: https://www.speedrun.com/smw/thread/f7cr2

In short:
1. Submit with the correct information
2. Submit with the correct time
3. Run on permitted platforms
4. Abide by the rules of the category
5. Provide a proper video/splits
6. Be patient

Additional rules for all speedruns:
1. No using save states, restore points, or rewinding
2. No speeding up or slowing down the game
3. No cheats (e.g. Game Genie, Action Replay, emulator cheats)
4. No memory viewing
5. No turbo buttons
6. Only bijectional remapping of buttons (see below)
7. No pressing left + right or up + down on the D-pad intentionally for any advantage

Button remapping:
You may remap your inputs, for example on Nintendo Switch or an emulator. However, you can only one key to any one button. You cannot map one key to simulate pressing more than one button on the console. Similarly, you cannot map multiple keys to the same button on the console.
This rule does not apply for the 0 Exit category.

categories.name: 96 Exit
categories.rules:
Time begins the frame Mario appears in the opening cutscene. This is 2.2 seconds after selecting 1 player game.
Time ends on the frame that Peach appears outside of Bowser's Clown Car.

- Clear every intended exit
- No Arbitrary Code Execution
- No Chuck Eat Item Swap related glitches (Orb/Cloud)

A post-run "file check" is **strongly encouraged**, but not required.

Milliseconds are **required** for times below 1:23:00.

categories.name: All Castles
categories.rules:
Time begins the frame Mario appears in the opening cutscene. This is 2.2 seconds after selecting 1 player game.
Time ends on the frame that Peach appears outside of Bowser's Clown Car.

- Complete all 8 castles as quickly as possible
- No Arbitrary Code Execution
- No Orb/Cloud
- No Submap Warp

Milliseconds are **required** for times below 35:00.

categories.name: No Starworld
categories.rules:
Time begins the frame Mario appears in the opening cutscene. This is 2.2 seconds after selecting 1 player game.
Time ends on the frame that Peach appears outside of Bowser's Clown Car.

- No Arbitrary Code Execution
- No Orb/Cloud
- No Starworld allowed
- No Submap Warp

Milliseconds are **required** for times below 33:00.

categories.name: 0 Exit
categories.rules:
Time begins the frame Mario appears in the opening cutscene. This is 2.2 seconds after selecting 1 player game.
Time ends when player loses control for credits warp. This is the first duplicate frame after performing the item swap (the frame before the screen starts to get darker).

- All glitches allowed

Video is required.

Milliseconds are **required** for all times.

(Also known as Credits Warp)

categories.name: 95 Exit, No Cape
categories.rules:
Time begins the frame Mario appears in the opening cutscene. This is 2.2 seconds after selecting 1 player game.
Time ends on the frame that Peach appears outside of Bowser's Clown Car.

- Complete every goal possible without a cape (Donut Ghost House, secret exit is not possible)
- No Arbitrary Code Execution
- No Cape
- No Chuck Eat Item Swap related glitches (Orb/Cloud)

Penalties:

- If a cape is obtained, die as soon as possible without utilizing it

A post-run "file check" is **strongly encouraged**, but not required.

Milliseconds are **required** for times below 1:27:00.

categories.name: All Castles, Small Only
categories.rules:
Time begins the frame Mario appears in the opening cutscene. This is 2.2 seconds after selecting 1 player game.
Time ends on the frame that Peach appears outside of Bowser's Clown Car.

- Complete all 8 castles as quickly as possible
- No Arbitrary Code Execution
- No Powerups allowed (Mushroom, Midway Points, Fire Flower, Cape)
- No Yoshi

Penalties:

- If any powerup is obtained, or Yoshi is ridden, die as soon as possible without utilizing it
- If a mushroom is gained by taking an item through the goal tape, die as soon as possible
- If you grab a checkpoint, take damage as soon as possible, finish the level, and then redo that same exit

Milliseconds are **required** for times below 40:00.

values.name: Cloud
values.rules:
Time begins the frame Mario appears in the opening cutscene. This is 2.2 seconds after selecting 1 player game.
Time ends on the frame that Peach appears outside of Bowser's Clown Car.

- No Credits Warp

*More specifically, no letting the instruction pointer hit anywhere but ROM, open bus, and the intended RAM area ($7F8000-$7F8182), and no modifying the intended RAM area.

Milliseconds are **required** for times below 13:00.

values.rules:
Glitchless rules:
- Clipping with or without yoshi is not allowed (unless accidental)

- It is **lightly recommended** to get yourself acquainted with using [therun.gg](https://therun.gg) for the purpose of connecting your LiveSplit program to the site to be able to show detailed data of your runs and attempts, as another way to provide validity to your runs.

If a runner is contacted about their submission, they will be expected to work with the mods and provide more proof if enough is not available. If the moderators do not believe that sufficient proof of skill is provided due to the above criteria not being met, they may reject the run.
